text: Cropmix / High-performance regular-grid backend Reference High-performance regular-grid backend Specialised utilities for large binary square lattices and adaptive Monte Carlo simulation. Scope # cropmix.publication_backend is a specialised computational module for large, regular square lattices. It represents two varieties as a binary N × N grid and avoids the dense pairwise movement matrix used by the geometry-general simulator. Use this module when its square-grid and two-variety assumptions match the problem; use the core Field , MixtureDesign and simulate_mixture() API for arbitrary coordinates or more than two varieties. StructuredKernel and preparation # StructuredKernel StructuredKernel(N, scale, balance, displacement_dr, displacement_dc, displacement_cdf, mean_step_distance, max_row_error, iterations) Matrix-free square-lattice kernel representation. prepare_structured_kernel prepare_structured_kernel(N, scale, *, tolerance=1e-8, max_iter=5000, damping=0.5) FFT-based symmetric balancing for an open N×N unit-spaced lattice. High-throughput SSA helpers # batch_publication_ssa batch_publication_ssa(N, cultivar, balance, drs, dcs, displacement_cdf, vectors_per_plant, initial_sites_table, observation_times, duration, event_seeds, acquisition, inoculation, gamma, rho, sigma, omega, clearance, yield_healthy, yield_infected) Numba-parallel low-level batch routine. Returns yields, final incidence, whole-field incidence, vector prevalence, SUSC incidence, RES incidence, final states and event counts. run_ensemble run_ensemble(*, N, cultivar, kernel, vectors_per_plant, initial_infectious, observation_times, duration, seed, acquisition, inoculation, gamma, rho, sigma, omega, clearance, yield_healthy, yield_infected, min_runs, max_runs, batch_size, final_incidence_mcse_tol, relative_yield_mcse_tol, fixed_sites=None, require_precision=True, store_infection_probability=False) Adaptive ensemble wrapper. Runs batches until minimum effort plus incidence/yield precision conditions are met (unless precision is disabled), and returns run arrays plus mean/SD/MCSE summaries, runtime, kernel diagnostics and optional infection probability. Seed and inoculum helpers # event_seeds event_seeds(seed, n) Generate deterministic per-run event seeds. random_initial_sites random_initial_sites(n_runs, n_sites, count, seed) Generate distinct random initial sites for each run. fixed_initial_sites fixed_initial_sites(n_runs, sites) Tile explicit initial sites across runs. mcse mcse(values) Sample SD / √n; returns infinity for fewer than two values. Binary-grid metrics # hni hni(grid) Moore-neighbour HNI. amd amd(grid) Average minimum heterospecific distance. local_diversity local_diversity(grid, window=3) Return local Shannon and Simpson means. ji_icm ji_icm(grid) Return juxtaposition and contagion/interspersion values. b2a b2a(grid) Boundary-to-area proxy using rook boundaries. patch_metrics patch_metrics(grid) Return patch density and mean patch area using 8-connectivity. morisita_horn morisita_horn(grid, block=5) Block Morisita–Horn overlap. coarse_transport_emd coarse_transport_emd(grid, block=5, epsilon_blocks=1.0) Entropically regularised block transport distance. ripley_cross_deviation ripley_cross_deviation(grid, rmax) Cross-Ripley-type deviation. compute_arrangement_metrics compute_arrangement_metrics(grid, *, rmax, local_window=3, mh_block=5, emd_block=5, emd_epsilon_blocks=1.0) Return the 12-metric dictionary. Design-ensemble helpers # correlated_exact_grid correlated_exact_grid(N, sigma, seed) Exact 50:50 binary grid from a Gaussian-filtered random field. generate_hni_target_ensemble generate_hni_target_ensemble(*, N, n_targets=25, replicates=8, seed=20260824, tolerance=5e-4) Generate exact 50:50 grids spanning HNI. Requires even N and returns grids plus a manifest dataframe. Choose the backend by model structure The geometry-general simulator and the regular-grid backend implement different computational representations. Select the regular-grid backend only when its binary square-lattice assumptions are scientifically appropriate.

text: Cropmix / Biological parameters User guide Biological parameters Define host, vector and pathogen parameters and propagate coherent transmission draws. Biological parameter objects # All core parameter containers are validated dataclasses. Rates are non-negative; the documented scientific convention is days. HostTransmission HostTransmission(acquisition_rate, inoculation_rate) Host-dependent acquisition rate (day⁻¹) and per-virus-bearing-vector inoculation rate (vector⁻¹ day⁻¹). PlantParameters PlantParameters(latent_progression_rate, roguing_rate=0.0) Plant latent progression and optional roguing/removal rate. YieldParameters YieldParameters(healthy, infected, unit="t/ha") Healthy and infected yields in one user-chosen non-empty unit. Variety Variety(name, transmission, plant, yield_model) Named host variety/phenotype combining transmission, plant and yield objects. Variety.with_transmission variety.with_transmission(transmission) Return an immutable copy with replaced transmission rates. VectorParameters VectorParameters(mortality_rate, dispersal_rate) Vector mortality/replacement and tagged-vector movement rates. PathogenParameters PathogenParameters(vector_clearance_rate, transmission_mode="SPT", vector_latent_progression_rate=None) Shared vector infectivity loss plus SPT/PT mode. PT requires a positive vector latent progression rate; the current spatial simulator still rejects PT. TransmissionDraw TransmissionDraw(acquisition_rates, inoculation_rates, vector_clearance_rate, vector_latent_progression_rate=None) One coherent parameter draw keyed by variety. Acquisition and inoculation dictionaries must contain exactly the same names; use this to preserve posterior dependence. CropMixSystem # CropMixSystem CropMixSystem(varieties, vector, pathogen, kernel=ExponentialKernel()) Combine one or more unique varieties, vector parameters, pathogen parameters and movement kernel. All varieties must share the same yield unit. CropMixSystem.from_iterable CropMixSystem.from_iterable(varieties, *, vector, pathogen, kernel=None) Build a system from any iterable of varieties. If kernel is omitted, ExponentialKernel() is used. CropMixSystem.variety system.variety(name) Return a named Variety; raises KeyError if absent. CropMixSystem.validate_design system.validate_design(design) Ensure every label in a design is represented in the system. CropMixSystem.ensure_spatial_supported system.ensure_spatial_supported() Raise UnsupportedModelError for non-SPT systems. CropMixSystem.with_kernel_scale system.with_kernel_scale(scale) Return a copy using the same biology and a new exponential-kernel scale. CropMixSystem.point_transmission_draw system.point_transmission_draw() Convert current point parameters into a coherent TransmissionDraw . System properties # Property Meaning variety_names Tuple of variety names in system order. variety_map Name → Variety dictionary. yield_unit Common yield unit. Parameter uncertainty # draw = cm.TransmissionDraw( acquisition_rates={"A":0.20, "B":0.10}, inoculation_rates={"A":0.08, "B":0.04}, vector_clearance_rate=0.5, ) result = cm.simulate_mixture( design, system, scenario, transmission_draw=draw, n_runs=200, seed=90, ) Joint rows matter When a TransmissionDraw comes from EpiPvr, preserve each joint posterior row. Do not independently shuffle acquisition, inoculation and clearance marginals.

headings: Purpose  Core biological objects  Movement and harvest choices  Example 100×100 field  Example scenario matrix  Spatial descriptors  Adapting the example
text: Cropmix / Worked example: cassava brown streak disease User guide Worked example: cassava brown streak disease A self-contained applied example using cassava brown streak disease (CBSD) to demonstrate a complete Cropmix workflow. CBSD is a whitefly-transmitted viral disease of cassava. This example illustrates how published biological rates, cultivar-specific yield effects, a spatial movement kernel and a defined epidemic introduction can be assembled into Cropmix objects. The numerical values belong to this worked example; users should provide parameters appropriate to their own crop–pathogen–vector system. Purpose # This example demonstrates how to construct a two-variety cassava system, define a spatial field and epidemic scenario, run stochastic simulations, and analyse arrangement effects. The same Cropmix objects can be used for other crop–pathogen–vector systems with parameters appropriate to the application. Core biological objects # import cropmix as cm SUSC = cm.Variety( "SUSC", cm.HostTransmission(15.31, 1.34), cm.PlantParameters(1/30, 0.0), cm.YieldParameters(31.0, 3.1, "t/ha"), ) RES = cm.Variety( "RES", cm.HostTransmission(4.84, 0.42), cm.PlantParameters(1/30, 0.0), cm.YieldParameters(25.0, 2.1, "t/ha"), ) SYSTEM = cm.CropMixSystem( (SUSC, RES), cm.VectorParameters(0.19, 0.45), cm.PathogenParameters(19.37, "SPT"), cm.ExponentialKernel(2.625), ) Movement and harvest choices # The primary Cropmix exponential scale is a=2.625 m , translating a published two-dimensional exponential mean distance of 5.25 m; the biological sensitivity interval is 0.5–5.75 m. The primary season is 300 days and the prespecified harvest-time sensitivity is 120, 180, 240, 300 and 360 days. Example 100×100 field # FIELD = cm.Field.rectangular(100,100,spacing=1.0) DESIGN = cm.MixtureDesign.random(FIELD, {"SUSC":5000, "RES":5000}, seed=20260824) SCENARIO = cm.Scenario( duration=300, vectors_per_plant=10, inoculum=cm.Inoculum.random(1), vector_inoculum=cm.VectorInoculum.none(), ) For large regular grids, the specialised structured backend is computationally preferable to the geometry-general dense movement matrix when its binary square-lattice assumptions match the design. Example scenario matrix # An analysis can compare several vector burdens and several initial infectious-plant counts. Labels such as LvLi or HvHi are optional user-defined experiment labels and are not part of the Cropmix API. Spatial descriptors # Spatial descriptors express arrangement effects through measurable properties such as local mixing, boundaries, aggregation, patch size and fragmentation, rather than relying only on the names of planting layouts. Adapting the example # Choose any supported field representation: rectangle, mask, polygon or directly supplied coordinates. Specify the required variety counts explicitly; mixture composition is user-defined. Declare every variety used by the SPT system in CropMixSystem. Choose plant and vector introductions independently through Inoculum and VectorInoculum. Optimise any exact count vector with a built-in or user-defined scalar objective. Do not transfer CBSD numbers blindly The CBSD movement scale, transmission rates, vector burden and yields are pathosystem-specific inputs. Reparameterise them for other crops/pathogens rather than treating them as software defaults.

title: Model & concepts
headings: Object hierarchy  Spatial CTMC  Plant infection  Vector acquisition  Plant progression  Vector loss  What is and is not inferred  Mean-field, branching process and spatial CTMC answer different questions
text: Cropmix / Model & concepts User guide Model & concepts The object model and continuous-time Markov chain used by Cropmix. Object hierarchy # The design deliberately separates concerns so that the same epidemic model can be reused across fields and crops. Layer Main object Responsibility Geometry Field Finite set of two-dimensional planting coordinates. Planting MixtureDesign Exactly one cultivar label per field coordinate. Host biology Variety Transmission, latency/roguing and healthy/infected yield. Vector/pathogen VectorParameters , PathogenParameters Vector mortality/movement and loss of infectivity / transmission mode. Movement ExponentialKernel Distance-weighted, symmetrically balanced non-local movement. System CropMixSystem Combines varieties, vector biology, pathogen biology and movement. Experiment Scenario Duration, vectors per plant and initial plant/vector infection pressure. Output SimulationResult Run-level stochastic trajectories, endpoint outcomes, maps and metadata. Spatial CTMC # For site i , the plant state is S (susceptible/uninfected), L (infected but not yet infectious) or I (infectious). The local vector population is partitioned into virus-free vectors and virus-bearing provenance classes. The key local invariant is: H i + Σ k V i (k) = m The principal state-changing events are inoculation, end of plant latency, optional roguing, acquisition, vector clearance, vector mortality/replacement and reciprocal vector exchange. Plant infection # A susceptible plant at site i becomes latent at a rate determined by its cultivar-specific inoculation parameter and the local number of virus-bearing vectors. Vector acquisition # Virus-free vectors on an infectious plant acquire infection at the cultivar-specific acquisition rate; their provenance class records the cultivar on which acquisition occurred. Plant progression # Latent plants progress to infectiousness at the cultivar-specific latent progression rate. Optional roguing returns infectious plants according to the specified roguing rate. Vector loss # Virus-bearing vectors can lose infectivity through clearance and through mortality/replacement, returning to the virus-free class. What is and is not inferred # Cropmix is a simulation and design framework. It does not automatically infer every biological parameter from spatial field outcomes. Acquisition, inoculation and clearance can be informed through EpiPvr access-period experiments; plant latency, yields and movement scale require their own evidence or experimental design. Transmission-mode limit The current spatial engine implements semi-persistent transmission (SPT). Persistent-transmission parameterisations that require an exposed/latent vector compartment are rejected rather than silently coerced into the SPT state space. Mean-field, branching process and spatial CTMC answer different questions # Cropmix keeps these modelling layers separate because they answer different questions. EpiPvr branching-process calculations concern establishment near invasion; the deterministic mean-field system is a well-mixed population reference; the spatial CTMC retains finite numbers, explicit coordinates, planting arrangement and stochasticity.

text: Cropmix / GitHub Pages deployment Reference GitHub Pages deployment Publish this static documentation under israeltankam.github.io/cropmix/. Target structure # You said the documentation will live in a subfolder of your personal GitHub Pages repository. This package is built for that exact structure: israeltankam.github.io/ ├── ... your existing personal site ... └── cropmix/ ├── index.html ├── getting-started.html ├── api.html ├── ... ├── assets/ ├── examples/ ├── sitemap.xml └── .nojekyll All internal links and assets are relative, so the site works under https://israeltankam.github.io/cropmix/ without a custom base-path configuration. Deploy by copying the folder # Unzip the website bundle. Copy the contained cropmix/ folder into the root of your israeltankam.github.io repository. Commit and push to the branch from which your personal site is served. Open https://israeltankam.github.io/cropmix/ and test navigation, search and code-copy buttons. Example Git commands # cd path/to/israeltankam.github.io cp -R path/to/unzipped/cropmix ./cropmix git add cropmix git commit -m "Add Cropmix documentation" git push Why .nojekyll is included # The site is plain static HTML/CSS/JavaScript and does not need Jekyll processing. The marker prevents Jekyll-specific filtering from interfering with static assets. Updating the documentation # Replace the folder contents with the new build, preserve relative paths, then commit. If the Python package version changes, update the version badge, API compatibility notes and examples before publishing. Optional source repository link # The current package metadata guide uses https://github.com/israeltankam/cropmix as the source repository. The website's “Source” button points there. text: Cropmix / EpiPvr integration User guide EpiPvr integration Infer transmission parameters from access-period experiments through the optional R bridge. Bridge architecture # Cropmix keeps the user workflow in Python while invoking an independently installed R/EpiPvr package through Rscript . Parameter inference can be SPT or PT; the full spatial Cropmix simulator remains SPT-only. Access-period data # AccessPeriodAssay AccessPeriodAssay(duration, tested, infected) One varying-access-period assay. All three sequences must have equal non-zero length; durations/tested are positive and 0 ≤ infected ≤ tested. AccessPeriodAssay.to_dataframe assay.to_dataframe() Return EpiPvr-style columns T_vec , R_vec , I_vec . AccessPeriodExperiment.spt AccessPeriodExperiment.spt(*, acquisition, inoculation, fixed_inoculation_for_acquisition, fixed_acquisition_for_inoculation, vectors_per_plant) Build an SPT experiment and its 2×2 fixed-duration matrix. AccessPeriodExperiment.pt AccessPeriodExperiment.pt(*, acquisition, latent, inoculation, fixed_when_acquisition_varies, fixed_when_latency_varies, fixed_when_inoculation_varies, vectors_per_plant) Build a PT experiment with AAP/LAP/IAP assays and a 3×3 fixed-duration matrix. AccessPeriodExperiment.write_bundle experiment.write_bundle(directory) Write AAP.csv, IAP.csv, optional LAP.csv, durations.csv and metadata.csv for the internal R bridge. Fit configuration and backend # EpiPvrFitOptions EpiPvrFitOptions(survival_upper_days=40.0, d_num_pts_pd=1, warmup=1000, iterations=2000, chains=4, parallel=0, seed=123) Validated R/Stan fit settings. EpiPvrFit # EpiPvrFit.posterior fit.posterior(*, unit="per_day") Return a copy of joint posterior rows. Rate columns are multiplied by 24 for per-day output; per_hour leaves them unchanged. EpiPvrFit.parameter_summary fit.parameter_summary(*, unit="per_day") Mean, median, sample SD, q05 and q95 for all *_rate columns. headings: Field: arbitrary 2-D planting coordinates  Field properties  MixtureDesign: one variety label per site  Design properties  Examples
text: Cropmix / Fields & planting designs User guide Fields & planting designs Represent regular or irregular planting coordinates and construct exact mixture assignments. Field: arbitrary 2-D planting coordinates # Field is the canonical geometry. It stores unique finite two-dimensional coordinates plus optional site IDs, a boundary, rectangular grid metadata and arbitrary metadata. Rectangles, masks and polygons are constructors around the same coordinate representation. Field Field(coordinates, site_ids=None, boundary=None, grid_shape=None, metadata={...}) Direct constructor. Coordinates must have shape (n_sites, 2) , be finite and unique. If site IDs are omitted, string IDs "0" , "1" , … are created. Field.rectangular Field.rectangular(rows, columns, *, spacing=1.0, origin=(0.0, 0.0)) Create a complete rectangle. spacing may be one scalar or (sx, sy) ; grid_shape is stored so designs can be reshaped. Field.from_coordinates Field.from_coordinates(coordinates, *, site_ids=None, boundary=None, metadata=None) Create a field from surveyed/custom coordinates; use this for irregular finite planting positions. Field.from_mask Field.from_mask(mask, *, spacing=1.0, origin=(0.0, 0.0)) Create sites at True cells of a 2-D Boolean mask. Site IDs are generated as r{row}c{col} . Field.from_polygon Field.from_polygon(boundary, *, spacing=1.0, origin=None) Generate a regular lattice clipped to a polygon. Boundary points are included by the point-in-polygon logic. Field.distance_matrix field.distance_matrix() Return the full pairwise Euclidean distance matrix. Field.site_index field.site_index(site_id) Resolve a site ID to its integer index; raises KeyError for an unknown ID. Field properties # Property Meaning coordinates Read-only (M,2) coordinate array. n_sites Number of planting positions. x , y Coordinate columns. extent (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) . site_ids Unique string IDs, one per site. boundary Optional polygon vertex array. grid_shape Set for complete rectangles; otherwise generally None . metadata User/constructor metadata dictionary. MixtureDesign: one variety label per site # MixtureDesign MixtureDesign(field, assignment) Create a design from an existing Field and exactly one non-empty variety label per site. MixtureDesign.random MixtureDesign.random(field, counts, *, seed=None) Shuffle an exact multiset of variety labels. Counts must be non-negative and sum exactly to field.n_sites . MixtureDesign.monoculture MixtureDesign.monoculture(field, variety) Fill every site with one variety. MixtureDesign.from_grid MixtureDesign.from_grid(grid, *, spacing=1.0) Create a complete rectangular field and design from a 2-D array of labels. MixtureDesign.from_dataframe MixtureDesign.from_dataframe(dataframe, *, x="x", y="y", variety="variety", site_id="site_id") Import x , y , variety and optionally site ID columns from pandas. MixtureDesign.to_dataframe design.to_dataframe() Export site ID, x, y and variety columns. MixtureDesign.as_grid design.as_grid() Reshape assignment into field.grid_shape . Only valid for complete rectangular fields. MixtureDesign.variety_indices design.variety_indices(variety) Return integer indices carrying the requested variety. MixtureDesign.swapped design.swapped(first, second) Return a new design with two labels exchanged; composition is preserved exactly. MixtureDesign.plot design.plot(ax=None, *, marker_size=80, legend=True) Scatter plot of cultivar assignment; requires cropmix[viz] . Design properties # Property Meaning n_sites Number of sites. varieties Sorted tuple of labels present in the design. counts Exact count dictionary. proportions Count divided by number of sites for each variety. assignment Immutable tuple of site labels. field Underlying Field. Examples # # Irregular surveyed field field = cm.Field.from_coordinates( [(0,0), (1.2,0.1), (2.4,0.0), (0.4,1.1), (1.8,1.3)], site_ids=["p1","p2","p3","p4","p5"], ) design = cm.MixtureDesign(field, ("A","A","B","C","B")) # Exact non-50:50 three-variety composition field2 = cm.Field.rectangular(20, 20) design2 = cm.MixtureDesign.random( field2, {"Elite":240, "Resistant":120, "Tolerant":40}, seed=17, ) print(design2.counts, design2.proportions) Exact composition MixtureDesign.random() accepts any exact count dictionary whose values sum to field.n_sites . The same design API covers monocultures, two-variety mixtures and mixtures containing three or more named varieties.

text: Cropmix / Getting started Getting started Getting started Install Cropmix, define a field and two varieties, run a stochastic epidemic and inspect the result. Requirements # Cropmix 0.2.0 requires Python 3.10 or newer and depends on NumPy, pandas, SciPy and Numba. Plotting is optional and is installed with the viz extra. python -m venv cropmix-env source cropmix-env/bin/activate # Windows: cropmix-env\Scripts\activate python -m pip install --upgrade pip python -m pip install cropmix If you are installing a local wheel instead of a registry release: python -m pip install ./dist/cropmix-0.2.0-py3-none-any.whl Optional extras # python -m pip install "cropmix[viz]" python -m pip install "cropmix[dev,viz,docs]" Check the installation # python -c "import cropmix; print(cropmix.__version__)" cropmix --version cropmix doctor cropmix doctor reports the Python environment and also checks for Rscript and EpiPvr when you plan to use the optional inference bridge. A complete minimal example # This example uses illustrative rate values. The units of all rates are per day; yields use an arbitrary but internally consistent unit. import cropmix as cm # 1. Planting coordinates field = cm.Field.rectangular(rows=6, columns=6, spacing=1.0) # 2. Host varieties variety_a = cm.Variety( name="A", transmission=cm.HostTransmission( acquisition_rate=0.80, inoculation_rate=0.25, ), plant=cm.PlantParameters( latent_progression_rate=1 / 18, roguing_rate=0.0, ), yield_model=cm.YieldParameters( healthy=1.0, infected=0.45, unit="relative yield", ), ) variety_b = cm.Variety( name="B", transmission=cm.HostTransmission( acquisition_rate=0.35, inoculation_rate=0.10, ), plant=cm.PlantParameters(latent_progression_rate=1 / 18), yield_model=cm.YieldParameters( healthy=0.90, infected=0.65, unit="relative yield", ), ) # 3. Vector, pathogen and movement model system = cm.CropMixSystem( varieties=(variety_a, variety_b), vector=cm.VectorParameters( mortality_rate=0.15, dispersal_rate=0.40, ), pathogen=cm.PathogenParameters( vector_clearance_rate=1.5, transmission_mode="SPT", ), kernel=cm.ExponentialKernel(scale=1.5), ) # 4. Exact planting composition # 36 sites = 18 plants of A + 18 plants of B design = cm.MixtureDesign.random( field, counts={"A": 18, "B": 18}, seed=7, ) # 5. Epidemic conditions scenario = cm.Scenario( duration=120, vectors_per_plant=5, inoculum=cm.Inoculum.random(count=1), vector_inoculum=cm.VectorInoculum.none(), ) # 6. Monte Carlo simulation result = cm.simulate_mixture( design, system, scenario, n_runs=50, seed=42, ) print(result.summary()) Random introductions are replicate-specific With Inoculum.random(count=1) , the initially infectious plant is sampled independently for each stochastic replicate. The global simulation seed makes the experiment reproducible. Inspect the result # print(result.mean_yield) print(result.yield_sd) # run-to-run variability print(result.yield_se) # Monte Carlo SE of the mean print(result.mean_final_incidence) trajectory = result.trajectory_dataframe() print(trajectory.head()) With plotting support installed: result.plot_incidence(by_variety=True) result.plot_vector_prevalence() result.plot_final_infection_probability() Where to go next # Change field geometry # Use surveyed coordinates, masks, polygons or dataframe import. Fields & planting designs → Change introductions # Use no plant inoculum, fixed infectious sites, vector infection pressure or combined introductions. Scenarios & inoculum → Analyse spatial structure # Use coordinate-based mixing metrics or regular-grid metrics where their assumptions apply. Spatial metrics → Optimise a design # Search the fixed-composition design space under expected yield or a custom objective. Optimisation →

text: Cropmix documentation Cropmix Spatial simulation and optimisation of crop varietal mixtures under vector-borne disease pressure. Python package Spatial CTMC Gillespie simulation Arbitrary 2-D fields Optimisation Cropmix provides a structured Python API for representing planting geometry, cultivar allocation, host traits, vector and pathogen parameters, epidemic introductions, stochastic simulation and spatial design analysis. Get started User guide API reference 0.2.0 Documentation for Cropmix 0.2.0 Requires Python 3.10 or newer. Optional extras provide plotting, documentation and development tools. What is Cropmix? # Cropmix is scientific software for studying how crop varietal composition and spatial arrangement interact with vector-borne disease dynamics. A workflow is assembled from explicit model objects rather than a single monolithic function: a Field defines planting coordinates, a MixtureDesign assigns varieties, a CropMixSystem defines biology and movement, and a Scenario defines the epidemic conditions. The same objects are reused for simulation, deterministic comparison and design optimisation. 1 Model fields and mixtures # Create rectangular grids, masks, polygon-clipped lattices or arbitrary coordinate sets. Assign exact variety counts or import an existing design. Fields & planting designs → 2 Simulate epidemics # Run finite stochastic continuous-time Markov chains with explicit plant states, vector infection status and non-local distance-weighted movement. Stochastic simulation → 3 Analyse spatial design # Summarise stochastic outcomes, compute spatial descriptors, compare spatial and mean-field dynamics, and search fixed-composition designs. Analysis workflows → Start here # Getting started # Install Cropmix and run a complete example from field construction to a SimulationResult . Installation and quickstart → User guide # Detailed explanations of geometry, biology, scenarios, movement, simulation, uncertainty, mean-field models, metrics and optimisation. Open the user guide → API reference # Signatures, properties and methods for the package root, submodules, optional EpiPvr bridge and regular-grid backend. Browse the API → Examples # Self-contained scripts for common workflows, including irregular fields, multi-variety mixtures, vector introductions and uncertainty analysis. Run the examples → Core workflow # Field planting coordinates → MixtureDesign variety at each site → CropMixSystem host + vector + pathogen + kernel → Scenario duration + introductions → SimulationResult trajectories + endpoints + maps Installation # python -m pip install cropmix Copy Until a PyPI release is available, install the wheel distributed with the project or install from a local clone. See Getting started . Scientific scope # The current spatial simulator implements semi-persistent transmission (SPT) with explicit plant latency and virus-bearing vectors. Parameter inference through the optional EpiPvr bridge can represent both SPT and persistent-transmission experiments; persistent-transmission spatial dynamics require an additional exposed-vector compartment and are therefore not simulated by the current engine. See Model boundaries for the complete scope.

title: Model boundaries
headings: Transmission model  Field size and movement matrices  Spatial metrics  Optimisation  Biological parameterisation  Vector burden  Yield model  Parameter uncertainty  Validation
text: Cropmix / Model boundaries Reference Model boundaries Current scientific and computational scope of Cropmix 0.2.0. Transmission model # The spatial simulator and deterministic mean-field solver implement semi-persistent transmission (SPT). PathogenParameters and the EpiPvr bridge can represent persistent-transmission (PT) parameter inference, but a PT CropMixSystem is rejected by the spatial simulator because PT dynamics require an explicit vector latent compartment. Field size and movement matrices # The geometry-general simulator supports arbitrary finite 2-D coordinates, but its movement preparation is dense and therefore scales quadratically in memory with the number of planting sites. The specialised cropmix.publication_backend avoids that dense matrix for large binary square lattices, at the cost of stricter geometry and variety assumptions. Spatial metrics # pairwise_mixing_metrics() is defined on arbitrary coordinates through an explicit distance radius. The 12 additional arrangement metrics in cropmix.publication_backend operate on binary square grids. Their definitions should not be applied to arbitrary geometry or multi-variety designs without an explicit extension. Optimisation # optimize_mixture() uses count-preserving simulated annealing. It is a heuristic search: the best returned design is the best design found under the declared objective, seed, Monte Carlo effort and annealing schedule, not a proof of a global optimum. Biological parameterisation # Cropmix consumes biological parameters; it does not infer every parameter from spatial epidemic data. Transmission parameters can be supplied directly or derived from access-period experiments through the optional EpiPvr bridge. Movement scale, plant progression, roguing and yield parameters require independent evidence appropriate to the target system. Vector burden # Scenario.vectors_per_plant is an integer model quantity. Mapping field vector observations to this quantity is part of study design and validation; the package does not automatically convert trap counts, visual counts or density indices into vectors per plant. Yield model # Each Variety supplies healthy and infected yield values in a user-chosen common unit. Cropmix 0.2.0 does not include mechanistic crop growth, infection-time-dependent yield loss, market prices or resource competition unless those are incorporated externally or through a custom optimisation objective. Parameter uncertainty # A simulation can receive one coherent TransmissionDraw . Full posterior predictive propagation is performed by an outer workflow that samples joint parameter draws and calls the simulator repeatedly; Cropmix does not silently resample marginal posterior distributions inside simulate_mixture() . Validation # Agreement between spatial and mean-field models is a model-consistency diagnostic, not empirical validation. Predictive validation requires independent biological parameterisation and spatial field observations.

title: Mean-field models
headings: Deterministic mean-field solver  MeanFieldResult  Mean-field adequacy diagnostic  MeanFieldConsistencyResult  Legacy alias
text: Cropmix / Mean-field models User guide Mean-field models Solve the deterministic reference model and assess when well-mixed dynamics approximate spatial simulations. Deterministic mean-field solver # solve_mean_field solve_mean_field(design, system, scenario, *, observation_times=None) Solve the generalized n-variety PLOS-style SPT reference with SciPy LSODA. Observation times default to 101 points. PT is not supported by this solver. MeanFieldResult # MeanFieldResult MeanFieldResult(time, latent, infectious, viruliferous_by_origin, variety_names, proportions, vector_burden, total_vectors, final_yield, yield_unit) Stores deterministic plant/vector trajectories and final yield. Property / method Meaning incidence Whole-field infectious fraction = sum of variety infectious states. vector_prevalence Total viruliferous vectors / total vectors. incidence_within_variety(name) Within-variety incidence; NaN if that variety has zero planted proportion. trajectory_dataframe() Time, overall incidence/vector prevalence, field infectious fraction and within-variety incidence columns. Mean-field adequacy diagnostic # assess_mean_field_consistency assess_mean_field_consistency(field, system, scenarios, *, reference_variety, scales=None, n_runs=50, observation_times=None, incidence_weight=0.5, vector_weight=0.5, bootstrap_reps=100, seed=20260810) Run a monoculture reference across multiple scenarios and movement scales, comparing mean spatial incidence/vector trajectories against mean field. Default scales are 100 log-spaced values from 0.05 to 100. The discrepancy is a weighted average of incidence RMSE and vector-prevalence RMSE. Final yield error is recorded as an external diagnostic but is not part of the score. The function reports a literal score-minimising scale, minimax scale, one-SE acceptable interval, a practical one-SE selected threshold and leave-one-context-out sensitivity. MeanFieldConsistencyResult # MeanFieldConsistencyResult MeanFieldConsistencyResult(...) Result object containing context_table , joint_table , context_optima , leave_one_context_out , scale summaries and score weights. Property / method Meaning acceptable_log10_width log10(acceptable_max / acceptable_min). boundary_warning True when the literal optimum lies at the scanned scale boundary. summary() One-row scale/diagnostic summary. plot() Mean/worst context discrepancy vs scale with one-SE interval and selected scale. Legacy alias # calibrate_kernel calibrate_kernel(*args, **kwargs) Deprecated alias that emits DeprecationWarning and forwards to assess_mean_field_consistency() . KernelCalibrationResult is also an alias of MeanFieldConsistencyResult . Scientific interpretation The selected scale is a threshold for practical mean-field adequacy in the tested contexts, not a biological estimate of insect movement. Use independent literature/tracking/spatial evidence for the biological kernel scale.

title: Spatial metrics
headings: Metric layers in Cropmix  Arbitrary-coordinate mixing  Binary square-grid descriptor set  Using metrics to generalise arrangement results  Exact equal-count binary grid generators
text: Cropmix / Spatial metrics User guide Spatial metrics Describe planting arrangement quantitatively so simulated outcomes can be interpreted in terms of spatial structure rather than layout names alone. A planting design can be described by measurable properties such as local heterospecific contact, aggregation, boundary density, fragmentation, patch size and second-order spatial structure. These descriptors provide a common numerical language for comparing arrangements and relating epidemic or yield outcomes to geometry. Metric layers in Cropmix # Cropmix provides two metric layers with different domains of validity. Layer Geometry Varieties Purpose cropmix.metrics.pairwise_mixing_metrics Any finite 2-D coordinates Any number of labels Local mixing within an explicit Euclidean radius. Regular-grid metric functions in cropmix.publication_backend Square binary NumPy grids Two labels coded 0/1 Richer descriptors of binary lattice structure. Arbitrary-coordinate mixing # pairwise_mixing_metrics cropmix.metrics.pairwise_mixing_metrics(design, *, radius) Two sites are neighbours when their Euclidean separation is greater than zero and no larger than radius . The function returns a pandas Series containing the radius, number of neighbour pairs, heterotypic-pair fraction and mean local heterospecific fraction. from cropmix.metrics import pairwise_mixing_metrics metrics = pairwise_mixing_metrics(design, radius=1.5) print(metrics) Binary square-grid descriptor set # The specialised regular-grid module provides twelve descriptors for binary square lattices. Function Descriptor Interpretation hni(grid) HNI Mean Moore-neighbour heterospecific fraction. amd(grid) AMD Mean distance to the nearest opposite label. local_diversity(grid, window=3) SH, SI Local Shannon and Simpson diversity. ji_icm(grid) JI, ICM Heterotypic adjacency and contagion/interspersion. b2a(grid) B2A Unlike horizontal/vertical boundary per site. patch_metrics(grid) FRAG, MPA 8-connected patch density and mean patch area. morisita_horn(grid, block=5) MH Block-scale Morisita–Horn overlap. coarse_transport_emd(...) EMD Entropically regularised coarse transport distance. ripley_cross_deviation(grid, rmax) RK Cross-Ripley-type deviation across integer radii. compute_arrangement_metrics compute_arrangement_metrics(grid, *, rmax, local_window=3, mh_block=5, emd_block=5, emd_epsilon_blocks=1.0) Return the complete descriptor dictionary with keys EMD , HNI , AMD , MH , SH , SI , JI , ICM , B2A , RK , FRAG and MPA . Using metrics to generalise arrangement results # Named arrangements are useful experimental designs, but their names are not mechanistic explanations. Spatial metrics translate those designs into measurable structural properties. This allows a user to ask whether simulated incidence or yield is associated with local mixing, boundary density, aggregation, patch size or another descriptor across several arrangements. A typical workflow is: generate or import a set of planting designs; compute the same descriptors for every design; simulate the outcome of interest under a common biological scenario; fit an interpretable model linking descriptors to outcomes; evaluate out-of-sample predictive performance and resampling stability before interpreting a metric or metric pair. Match the metric to the geometry A spatial concept can be useful beyond binary square grids, but the numerical definition must be valid for the target geometry and number of varieties. Use the arbitrary-coordinate metric for general fields, or define an explicit extension before applying binary-grid descriptors outside their stated scope. Exact equal-count binary grid generators # The regular-grid module includes two utilities for constructing equal-count binary grids. correlated_exact_grid correlated_exact_grid(N, sigma, seed) Create an exact equal-count binary N × N grid from a Gaussian-filtered random field. generate_hni_target_ensemble generate_hni_target_ensemble(*, N, n_targets=25, replicates=8, seed=20260824, tolerance=5e-4) Create exact equal-count binary grids spanning the HNI mixing axis. N must be even. Returns a grid dictionary and a manifest dataframe.

title: Vector movement
headings: Core exponential kernel  PreparedKernel  Low-level balancing helper  Dense kernel audit  Structured kernel for large square grids  Biological interpretation of scale
text: Cropmix / Vector movement User guide Vector movement Configure the exponential movement kernel and inspect finite-field balancing diagnostics. Core exponential kernel # ExponentialKernel ExponentialKernel(scale=1.0, balance_tolerance=1e-11, balance_max_iter=20000) Raw weights follow exp(-d/scale) . Scale, balancing tolerance and iteration limit must be positive. ExponentialKernel.with_scale kernel.with_scale(scale) Return an immutable copy with a new positive scale. ExponentialKernel.prepare kernel.prepare(field) Compute the full dense distance matrix, raw weights, symmetric balanced movement probabilities, CDF and finite-field diagnostics. W ij = exp(−d ij /a), W ii =0 The prepared probabilities are symmetric and row-stochastic. In the conservative vector-exchange generator, reciprocal exchanges preserve exactly m vectors at each site. PreparedKernel # PreparedKernel PreparedKernel(scale, probabilities, distances, cdf, mean_step_distance, max_row_error, max_symmetry_error) Dense finite-field movement object returned by ExponentialKernel.prepare() . Arrays are made read-only. Field Meaning probabilities Balanced row-stochastic symmetric matrix P. distances Pairwise Euclidean distance matrix. cdf Row-wise destination CDF. mean_step_distance Mean movement distance after finite-field balancing. max_row_error Maximum |row sum − 1|. max_symmetry_error Maximum |P − Pᵀ|. Low-level balancing helper # symmetric_sinkhorn cropmix.kernels.symmetric_sinkhorn(weights, *, tol=1e-11, max_iter=20000) Balance a symmetric non-negative square matrix to a reciprocal doubly/row-stochastic matrix. This is a submodule helper, not exported from the package root. Dense kernel audit # import numpy as np field = cm.Field.rectangular(8, 8) k = cm.ExponentialKernel(2.625).prepare(field) P = k.probabilities assert np.max(np.abs(P.sum(axis=1)-1)) < 1e-10 assert np.max(np.abs(P-P.T)) < 1e-10 assert np.max(np.abs(np.diag(P))) < 1e-12 print(k.mean_step_distance, k.max_row_error, k.max_symmetry_error) Structured kernel for large square grids # The geometry-general simulator uses a dense PreparedKernel. For large regular square lattices, cropmix.publication_backend provides a structured representation that avoids materialising the full pairwise movement matrix. publication_backend.prepare_structured_kernel prepare_structured_kernel(N, scale, *, tolerance=1e-8, max_iter=5000, damping=0.5) Prepare symmetric finite-field balancing on an open N×N unit-spaced lattice using FFT convolution and return a StructuredKernel. from cropmix.publication_backend import prepare_structured_kernel structured = prepare_structured_kernel(N=100, scale=2.625) print(structured.mean_step_distance, structured.max_row_error, structured.iterations) Dense and structured kernels are different representations PreparedKernel is used by the arbitrary-coordinate core simulator. StructuredKernel is specialised to large square lattices and should be used through the regular-grid backend. Biological interpretation of scale # The movement scale must come from independent biological evidence. Mean-field consistency asks when a non-spatial approximation becomes adequate; it does not estimate vector dispersal biology.

title: Optimisation
headings: Exact optimiser API  Built-in objectives  Common random numbers  Annealing and final evaluation  OptimizationResult  Examples
text: Cropmix / Optimisation User guide Optimisation Search fixed-composition planting designs with count-preserving simulated annealing. Exact optimiser API # OptimizationConfig OptimizationConfig(iterations=500, n_runs_per_candidate=20, final_runs=500, initial_temperature=0.5, cooling_rate=0.99, seed=12345, final_seed_offset=50000000) Validated settings for swap-based simulated annealing. Iterations may be zero; replication counts and temperature must be positive; cooling rate lies in (0,1]. optimize_mixture optimize_mixture(field, variety_counts, system, scenario, *, objective="expected_yield", config=None, initial_design=None, transmission_draw=None) Search arrangements while preserving exact counts. If no initial design is supplied, an exact-count random design is generated using the config seed. Built-in objectives # Name Internal score (maximised) expected_yield result.mean_yield min_final_incidence -result.mean_final_incidence yield_stability result.mean_yield - result.yield_sd You may also pass any callable f(SimulationResult) -> float . A custom objective can therefore include economic costs or risk penalties as long as larger values mean better designs. Common random numbers # All candidate designs in one optimisation use the same simulation seed block ( config.seed + 1,000,000 ). This induces paired stochastic noise and improves precision of design differences. Evaluated assignments are cached so identical designs are not simulated twice. Annealing and final evaluation # Each proposal swaps two heterotypic labels. Improvements are accepted; worse scores may be accepted with probability exp(delta/temperature) . The temperature is geometrically cooled. The best design found is then re-simulated with config.final_runs using config.seed + final_seed_offset , with final states retained. OptimizationResult # OptimizationResult OptimizationResult(best_design, best_score, final_result, history, objective_name, variety_counts, evaluations) Stores the best found design and search trace. history has iteration, current_score, best_score, accepted and temperature columns; evaluations is the number of unique designs actually simulated. OptimizationResult.summary result.summary() Insert objective name, optimization score and evaluation count into the final SimulationResult summary. Examples # config = cm.OptimizationConfig( iterations=1000, n_runs_per_candidate=30, final_runs=1000, cooling_rate=0.995, seed=123, ) opt = cm.optimize_mixture( field, {"A":60, "B":40}, system, scenario, objective="expected_yield", config=config, ) print(opt.summary()) # User-defined risk-adjusted objective def risk_adjusted(r): return r.mean_yield - 2.0*r.yield_sd opt2 = cm.optimize_mixture(field, {"A":60,"B":40}, system, scenario, objective=risk_adjusted) Heuristic result, not proof The fixed-count design space is combinatorial. best_design means best found under the declared objective, seed, candidate-run count and annealing schedule; it is not a certified global optimum.

headings: Core complexity  Choose the computational path by geometry  First-call compilation  Adaptive Monte Carlo  Cluster execution
text: Cropmix / Performance & HPC Reference Performance & HPC Choose the appropriate computational backend and run large workloads reproducibly. Core complexity # The geometry-general simulate_mixture() calls ExponentialKernel.prepare(field) , which builds pairwise distances, movement probabilities and a CDF. Memory therefore scales quadratically with the number of sites. The Numba event loop is fast after compilation, but it does not remove dense-kernel memory. Choose the computational path by geometry # Problem structure Recommended path Irregular, surveyed, masked or polygonal field Geometry-general simulate_mixture() . Small to moderate regular grid Geometry-general simulator; simplest path and full core API. Large binary square lattice cropmix.publication_backend.prepare_structured_kernel() with run_ensemble() . First-call compilation # The first simulation in a Python process pays Numba compilation cost. Subsequent calls reuse compiled functions when possible. Time software benchmarking only after a warm-up call if you want steady-state performance. Adaptive Monte Carlo # The regular-grid backend accumulates batches from min_runs to max_runs , checks final-incidence MCSE and yield MCSE relative to the mean, and can retain site infection probabilities. This is preferable to picking a nominal run count without precision auditing. Cluster execution # For long-running ensembles, use a batch scheduler such as SLURM, write results incrementally, and cache completed scenario/design combinations so interrupted jobs can resume without repeating finished work. # Generic SLURM pattern from the delivered cluster workflow sbatch slurm_100x100.sbatch squeue -u "$USER" tail -f cropmix_100x100_<jobid>.log Regular-grid backend is specialised Its efficiency comes partly from assuming a square binary two-variety lattice. It is not a drop-in replacement for arbitrary geometry or arbitrary numbers of varieties.

text: Cropmix / Reproducibility & QA Reference Reproducibility & QA Seeds, environment checks, testing and release practices for repeatable analyses. Freeze the full scientific state # Archive package version, Python/platform/library versions, field coordinates, design assignment, biological parameters, scenario, movement scale, seeds, observation times and all analysis-level Monte Carlo stopping rules. Seed semantics # Random plant introductions and epidemic events are stochastic within a reproducible master-seed schedule. Reusing one seed across competing designs is deliberate common-random-number pairing, not a request for identical trajectories. Required numerical invariants # Field coordinates are finite and unique. Design labels exactly match field size and all labels are present in CropMixSystem. Dense prepared kernel has row sums ≈1, symmetry ≈0 error and zero diagonal. Vector-count invariant holds during every compiled simulation. Exact cultivar counts are checked before and after optimisation swaps. SPT/PT boundary is enforced rather than silently approximated. Stochastic SD and MCSE are labelled separately. Joint EpiPvr rows stay joint through propagation. Tests run against the source snapshot used here # This documentation was audited against the exact Cropmix 0.2.0 source embedded in Final_robust_complete_revised_2026-08-24.zip . Running its full extracted test directory in this session gave: PYTHONPATH=src NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=2 pytest -q # 17 passed, 1 deprecation warning (calibrate_kernel alias) The website additionally checks that every documented package-root export and EpiPvr export appears in the API inventory, that internal HTML links resolve, and that the final ZIP passes an archive integrity test. Release commands # python -m compileall -q src pytest -q ruff check src tests python -m build python -m twine check dist/* Versioned analyses Record the Cropmix version, dependency environment, random seeds, parameter sources and analysis code used to generate results. text: Cropmix / Results & uncertainty User guide Results & uncertainty Interpret replicate-level outcomes, trajectories, variability, maps and exports. SimulationResult data fields # Cropmix retains expensive run-level stochastic information so uncertainty can be recomputed without rerunning the epidemic. Field Shape / meaning design , scenario Input objects. time Observation times. yield_runs One realised yield per run. final_incidence_runs One final infectious fraction per run. incidence_runs Run × time whole-field incidence. vector_prevalence_runs Run × time virus-bearing-vector prevalence. incidence_by_variety_runs Name → run × time within-variety incidence. final_states Run × site final state codes, or None. infection_probability Site-wise P(infectious at T), or None when final states were not stored. kernel_scale , mean_step_distance Movement provenance. seed , yield_unit Reproducibility and units. Summary properties # mean_yield result.mean_yield Mean of yield_runs . yield_sd result.yield_sd Sample SD of run-level yield; zero for one run. yield_se result.yield_se Yield SD / √n, the Monte Carlo standard error of mean yield. mean_final_incidence result.mean_final_incidence Mean endpoint infectious fraction. final_incidence_sd result.final_incidence_sd Sample SD of final incidence. mean_incidence result.mean_incidence Pointwise mean incidence. incidence_sd result.incidence_sd Pointwise sample SD of incidence; zero array for one run. mean_vector_prevalence result.mean_vector_prevalence Pointwise mean vector prevalence. vector_prevalence_sd result.vector_prevalence_sd Pointwise sample SD of vector prevalence. incidence_by_variety_sd result.incidence_by_variety_sd Name → pointwise within-variety SD; all-NaN varieties remain NaN. Methods # SimulationResult.summary result.summary() One-row dataframe containing n_runs, mean/SD/SE yield, mean/SD final incidence, kernel scale and mean step distance. SimulationResult.trajectory_dataframe result.trajectory_dataframe() Tidy dataframe with time, means, SDs and clipped ±1 SD lower/upper envelopes for field incidence, vector prevalence and each variety. SimulationResult.plot_incidence result.plot_incidence(ax=None, *, by_variety=False, show_sd=True, sd_multiplier=1.0, envelope_alpha=0.2) Plot field incidence and optionally cultivar trajectories. SD envelopes are shown by default; requires viz extra. SimulationResult.plot_vector_prevalence result.plot_vector_prevalence(ax=None, *, show_sd=True, sd_multiplier=1.0, envelope_alpha=0.2) Plot mean vector prevalence with optional SD band. SimulationResult.plot_final_infection_probability result.plot_final_infection_probability(ax=None, *, marker_size=100) Scatter field coordinates coloured by site-level final infection probability. Requires final states and viz extra. Export stochastic trajectories # result.summary().to_csv("summary.csv", index=False) result.trajectory_dataframe().to_csv("trajectories.csv", index=False) # Raw arrays remain available for quantiles, paired comparisons, etc. q05, q50, q95 = np.quantile(result.final_incidence_runs, [0.05,0.5,0.95]) Do not discard raw runs The corrected package exposes SDs and ±SD envelopes, but the raw run arrays remain the primary information. Preserve them when storage permits.

title: Scenarios & inoculum
headings: Scenario  Plant inoculum  Vector inoculum  Examples
text: Cropmix / Scenarios & inoculum User guide Scenarios & inoculum Specify simulation horizon, vector burden and plant/vector introductions. Scenario # Scenario Scenario(duration=300.0, vectors_per_plant=10, inoculum=Inoculum(), vector_inoculum=VectorInoculum()) Field-level conditions. Duration and vectors per plant must be positive. The default is one random infectious plant and virus-free vectors. A disease-free control with zero infected plants and zero infectious vectors is explicitly valid in the 0.2.0 source. Plant inoculum # Inoculum Inoculum(count=1, sites=None) If sites=None , choose count distinct random sites independently for each replicate. Explicit sites fix the introduction location. Inoculum.random Inoculum.random(count=1) Random plant introduction. Inoculum.fixed Inoculum.fixed(sites) Fixed, unique integer site indices. Inoculum.none Inoculum.none() Zero infectious plants. Vector inoculum # VectorInoculum VectorInoculum(infectious_fraction=0.0, origin_weights=None) Initial probability that each individual vector is virus-bearing. infectious_fraction lies in [0,1]. Optional non-negative origin_weights are normalised across system varieties; when omitted, planted variety frequencies are used for provenance. VectorInoculum.none VectorInoculum.none() All vectors virus-free at time zero. Examples # # One random infectious plant; virus-free vectors s1 = cm.Scenario(300, 10, cm.Inoculum.random(1), cm.VectorInoculum.none()) # Five random infectious plants s2 = cm.Scenario(300, 5, cm.Inoculum.random(5), cm.VectorInoculum.none()) # Fixed plant introductions s3 = cm.Scenario(120, 4, cm.Inoculum.fixed([12, 50, 87]), cm.VectorInoculum.none()) # Vector-only introduction: 2% of vectors initially virus-bearing s4 = cm.Scenario(60, 4, cm.Inoculum.none(), cm.VectorInoculum(infectious_fraction=0.02)) # Combined sources s5 = cm.Scenario(180, 8, cm.Inoculum.random(2), cm.VectorInoculum(infectious_fraction=0.05)) # Disease-free control control = cm.Scenario(30, 3, cm.Inoculum.none(), cm.VectorInoculum.none()) Random means random per replicate For random inoculum, the simulator uses a reproducible but replicate-specific draw of distinct site indices. Reusing the master seed recreates the sequence; it does not force the same plant to be infected in every run.

headings: Exact public signature  Arguments  State process  Random introductions and seeds  Example with explicit observation times and posterior draw  Performance boundary of the core simulator  Monte Carlo precision
text: Cropmix / Stochastic simulation User guide Stochastic simulation Run the spatial continuous-time Markov chain with Gillespie simulation. Exact public signature # simulate_mixture simulate_mixture(design, system, scenario, *, n_runs=100, seed=12345, observation_times=None, transmission_draw=None, store_final_states=True) Run replicated finite spatial SPT Gillespie trajectories. There is no engine or backend argument in the frozen 0.2.0 core source. Arguments # Argument Behaviour design Any valid MixtureDesign using system varieties. system CropMixSystem; PT is rejected by the spatial engine. scenario Duration, vectors per plant, plant and vector introductions. n_runs Positive number of Monte Carlo replicates. seed Master seed. Reuse across candidate designs for common-random-number comparisons. observation_times Sorted non-empty 1-D times within [0,duration]. Default: 101 equally spaced points. transmission_draw Optional coherent TransmissionDraw; otherwise system point values are used. store_final_states If false, final state arrays and infection-probability map are discarded after summaries are computed. State process # Plants occupy S, L or I states. Virus-bearing vectors are tracked at each site by acquisition-origin variety. Events include plant inoculation, latent progression, roguing, vector acquisition, vector loss of infectivity, vector mortality/replacement and conservative non-local exchange. Random introductions and seeds # With Inoculum.random(k) , distinct sites are redrawn independently for each replicate using a deterministic seed schedule. Event seeds are also replicate-specific. Reusing the same master seed across designs provides paired stochastic input streams for comparative design evaluation. Example with explicit observation times and posterior draw # import numpy as np times = np.unique(np.r_[np.linspace(0,300,61), 120,180,240,300]) result = cm.simulate_mixture( design, system, scenario, n_runs=500, seed=20260824, observation_times=times, transmission_draw=draw, # optional; omit to use point parameters store_final_states=True, ) Performance boundary of the core simulator # The geometry-general simulator prepares pairwise distances and a dense finite-field movement matrix. This is convenient and auditable for arbitrary moderate-sized fields, but memory grows quadratically with the number of planting sites. For large regular square lattices, cropmix.publication_backend provides a specialised structured representation when its binary-grid assumptions are appropriate. Monte Carlo precision # simulate_mixture() uses a fixed n_runs . The specialised publication_backend.run_ensemble() adds adaptive batching and checks Monte Carlo precision for final incidence and yield before stopping, subject to configured minimum and maximum run counts. SD vs SE/MCSE Stochastic standard deviation describes run-to-run variability. SimulationResult.yield_se is the Monte Carlo standard error of the mean yield. Do not report these as interchangeable uncertainty measures.
